collection.question: Can the Winchester Water Treatment Plant be expanded from its current 12 mgd to 18 mgd? For each unit along the flow path, determine whether it limits 18 mgd, the flow at which it becomes limiting, and the least-cost modification that makes 18 mgd work.

rfi.issue: RFI-01 Intake true bottleneck: 16 nominal vs 15.0 (2002) vs 14 (2006 Pumps 1,2,4) - is Pump 3 failed or is it high TDH/low river/fouled intake?
rfi.reason: Cannot size 18-mgd firm (replace Pump 1 4->6 mgd + VFD + screens) without knowing if deficit is pump degradation or system head; cleaning state and river level at tests unknown
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Deficit is combination of Pump 3 degradation plus fouled intake/high TDH; assume cleaning + Pump 1 upsizing + VFD + new fish screens achieves 18 mgd firm; verify by test. Reason: report directs clean before retest and replace/repair malfunctioning pumps (p.109).

rfi.issue: RFI-02 Raw 30-in pipeline length, profile, minor losses and TDH at 18-24 mgd missing; Table 4-1 only ft/100 ft
rfi.reason: Headloss in ft and velocity-head cannot be totalled to check 49-ft TDH margin and 6 fps criterion without length/fittings
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use Table 4-1 unit losses (p.110) times field-measured length; assume short length so surge minimal and higher velocity >6 fps acceptable with higher-head pumps. Reason: report states short length + valve/fitting config = minimal surge even >18 mgd (p.110).

rfi.issue: RFI-03 Pretreatment treatment basis withheld (G, detention, SOR, weir loading, rapid-mix power) - Sec 2/3 not in available pages
rfi.reason: 12 mgd rating and 18 mgd two-basin nominal cannot be checked against standards; only hydraulic levels given
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept stated ratings 12 mgd single / 18 mgd nominal two basins same media / ~24 mgd hydraulic (p.111) as treatment criteria. Reason: some recommendation clauses withheld; reach conclusions from facts; treatment review needs raw turbidity/temperature performance data.

rfi.issue: RFI-04 Single-basin emergency at 18 mgd: max WS 466.0 at 12 mgd, launder invert 465.83, trough bottom 464.63, overflow 465.0/9 ft/12 mgd at 9-in, drain 30-in 10 mgd - freeboard and weir binding flow unknown
rfi.reason: Need to know at what flow 1.5-ft freeboard or overflow weir binds with one vs two basins; second overflow for 24 mgd not yet built
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: With two basins in parallel freeboard adequate to 18 mgd; single basin limited ~12 mgd by overflow weir/drain. Reason: report says second weir with second basin adequate to 24 mgd ultimate (p.111) and careful yard piping may avoid raising existing weir (p.112).

rfi.issue: RFI-05 42-in settled pipe total headloss at 18-24 mgd: only one point 2.8-in at 13.1 mgd (2006) plus 6-in margin to overflow; length/tie-in unknown
rfi.reason: Calibration needs length and second flow; ultimate 22-24 mgd limit by this pipe (p.112) cannot be located without profile
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Calibrate coefficient to 2.8-in at 13.1 mgd test (p.111) and drawing WS 464.83 vs 465.00; assume shortened yard piping in expansion as report directs. Reason: report requires careful layout to reduce full-flow length (p.111-p.112).

rfi.issue: RFI-06 Filter rating basis missing: media type/depth/area/loading rate, 3 mgd/filter state standard vs pilot; hydraulically 4 mgd/filter stated without headloss curve
rfi.reason: Cannot confirm 6x3=18 mgd treatment vs 6x4=24 mgd hydraulic without Sec 2 data; driving head 15-17.5 ft and 11-ft alarm need curve
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept 3 mgd/filter treatment, 4 mgd/filter hydraulic to clearwell (p.112) as criteria. Reason: stated as treatment not hydraulic limitation; expansion adds two filters same media.

rfi.issue: RFI-07 Filter effluent meter 7% low, straight-pipe noncompliance; filter-to-waste ~2 mgd limit by difference calc (9.1 mgd raw minus Filters 2+4) - both uncertain
rfi.reason: Flow split and 3-mgd-to-waste requirement cannot be proven; sample point prohibits turbidity during to-waste
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Meters read 7% low (p.112); 8-in to-waste limited to ~2 mgd (p.112-p.113); reconfiguration needed to pass/control 3-4 mgd to waste. Reason: report estimates by difference and recommends reconfiguration for greatest benefit (p.113).

rfi.issue: RFI-08 Clearwell usable volume vs total 627k (712k with Filters 5-6); 1-ft backwash drop, minimum level for CT/wetwell, CT compliance at 12/18 mgd in Sec 3 missing
rfi.reason: 75 min at 12 mgd and 57 min at 18 mgd assume entire volume available (p.114-p.115) which report says overstates; disinfection evaluation withheld
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Total volumes 627k/712k at 10.5 ft (p.114-p.115) with 1-ft backwash penalty; CT adequacy to be checked in treatment step using Sec 3 baffling factors. Reason: report flags actual < total and defers to treatment evaluation.

rfi.issue: RFI-09 High service system head to Reservoir Hill (Elev 710 dwg) and pump curves missing; nominal firm 10 vs true 11.5 (3300 gpm ea) vs max 16/14 actual
rfi.reason: Cannot confirm 305-ft TDH pumps + new 6(VFD)+4 mgd (Table 4-2) deliver 18 mgd firm against 1986-system head without curves/HGL
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Accept Table 4-2 expansion (retain 1-4 add 6-VFD +4 in existing spaces) achieves 18 mgd firm (p.116). Reason: spaces exist; VFDs balance clearwell; >18 mgd needs higher head/system study (p.117-p.118).

rfi.issue: RFI-10 Finished-water transmission total capacity: 1986 study, Phase 1 done, Phase 2 27-in/30-in/second 30-in status and master-plan update pending; WTP-site segment length missing
rfi.item: Finished transmission WTP to Reservoir Hill
rfi.reason: Table 4-3 only ft/100 ft; 18-mgd two-pipe adequacy depends on whether second 30-in built prior/concurrent (p.118)
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: WTP-site short segment acceptable >6 fps (p.116-p.117); off-site needs Phase 2/second 30-in per 1986 plan as determined by master plan. Reason: report says further analysis outside scope + update study if >18 mgd (p.118).

rfi.issue: RFI-11 Surge tank replacement size for >14 mgd missing; existing 1900 cf/14200 gal only to 9700 gpm/14 mgd
rfi.reason: Cannot size larger tank without transient model to 18-24 mgd and 150 psi / HGL 630 ft criteria
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Existing adequate only to 14 mgd; expansion beyond existing total pumping requires larger tank, second tank impractical (p.117). Reason: space constraint stated; size by surge study.

rfi.issue: RFI-12 Backwash waste path capacity: 24-in to 30-in, open channel under gallery, diversion MH weir, WWPS firm 3000 gpm vs backwash 3250 (4060 tested, 4400 deep-bed optimum) plus settled sludge/coincident flows
rfi.reason: Firm 3000 gpm < single backwash rate; channel hydraulics and simultaneous filter + sedimentation overflow not quantified
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Existing backwash pumps/piping adequate for existing media to 18 mgd with one pump duty/one standby; upsize 24-in to 30-in with new filters (p.119); assess downstream channel/WWPS/solids for >18 mgd deep bed. Reason: report states adequate for existing config/type (p.119).

rfi.issue: RFI-13 Solids handling adequacy at 18 mgd: 2x300k gal basins +2 beds, decant rate, solids load, drying time, river overflow constraints missing
rfi.reason: Cannot confirm 600k gal equalization handles 260-300k gal/day backwash + sludge at 18 mgd with decant/overflow to river
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Recently built 2x300k gal +2 beds adequate to 18 mgd with alternating fill/decant; verify by solids balance. Reason: new facilities replace lagoon (p.119); detailed residuals analysis needed.

rfi.issue: RFI-14 Drawing elevations partly single-read/illegible in available scan; need confirmation before profile calibration
rfi.reason: Two independent reads required; several labels (466.0, 465.99, 464.83, 464.0, 449.0, 449.5, 710.0 etc.) need field/owner confirmation per rules
rfi.resolution: ASSUMPTION: Use text elevations (466.0, 465.83, 464.63, 465.0, 449.0, 449.5, 450.00) from p.111-p.114 as controlling; treat dwg WS as calibration targets to be confirmed. Reason: text and drawing should agree; report residuals at design flow.
